param.label: Percentiles of the contact frequency data to saturate the image
param.help: Comma separated, e.g. 0.95,0.96,0.97,0.98,0.99. If not set, those five percentiles are used.

validator.message: Comma separated numbers between 0 and 1, e.g. 0.95,0.96,0.97

param.label: Raw p-value cutoff for the final call set

tool.help:
Stripe detection =================
**hicDetectStripes** detects architectural stripes: one-sided, extended contact domains anchored near a boundary and extending along one axis (typically associated with loop extrusion stalling at a single CTCF site), as opposed to the two-sided point interactions ``hicDetectLoops`` finds.
New in HiCExplorer v4: a faithful reimplementation of Stripenn's own detection method (Yoon et al. 2022), not an invented stand-in. HiCExplorer's own Python releases, including the 2020 Galaxy HiCExplorer publication, had no stripe caller.
_________________
Usage -----
The candidate search scans each chromosome at several contact-frequency saturation percentiles (*Percentiles of the contact frequency data to saturate the image*), runs Canny edge detection, and looks for extended, roughly axis-aligned runs of edge pixels anchored near the diagonal. *Maximum stripe width* bounds the narrow (anchor) axis; *Shortest candidate stripe length* is the minimum extent along the long axis. Each candidate is scored against an empirical background model built from random same-distance samples of the chromosome's own data (*Random samples per chromosome*) and filtered at either a raw p-value or a Benjamini-Hochberg q-value (FDR) cutoff.
Matching Stripenn's own practice, no multiple-testing correction is applied by default (the raw p-value cutoff); the stricter FDR cutoff is available as an alternative.
_________________
Output ------
The output is a tab separated file, one row per detected stripe: chromosome, anchor start, anchor end, orientation ("horizontal" when the narrow axis sits near the start of the long axis, "vertical" when it sits near the end), extent start, extent end, enrichment (mean contact value over the stripe divided by the chromosome's expected value at its offset from the diagonal; contact values are the matrix balanced with its stored weights, as in Stripenn), p-value and q-value.
_________________
For more information about HiCExplorer please consider our documentation on readthedocs.io_.
.. _readthedocs.io: http://hicexplorer.readthedocs.io/en/latest/index.html
